scene.title: Find the loose rebound first
scene.objective: Separate a loose puck from a promised rebound goal.
scene.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x); gold attacks the left net. The coach states that F1’s previous shot came loose to the goalie’s side. YOU are arriving away from the puck. No goal or next touch is assumed.
cues: The loose puck is on the positive-y side of the goal area.
D1 stands closer to the middle.
YOU must locate the puck before planning a second action.

scene.title: Use the half wall to change the passing route
scene.objective: Distinguish a blocked direct line from an unproven indirect wall option.
scene.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x); gold attacks the left net. F1 has the puck near the half wall, the side-board area partway into the attacking zone. D1 stands directly between F1 and YOU. Consider an indirect pass using the boards; no bounce has been simulated.
cues: D1 blocks the straight F1-to-YOU line.
The side boards offer a different possible route.
D2 remains nearer the middle and goal.

question.prompt: Which two cues shape the bank point?

options.text: Where YOU can receive the rebound
Whether D2 remains available at the opposite point

question.explanation: The rebound location and D2’s opposite-point support determine whether the wall changes the useful route; D2’s stillness alone does not.

scene.title: Recover the pass that missed
scene.objective: Update a receiving plan after the puck goes beyond the intended target.
scene.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x); gold attacks the left net. F1’s pass has missed YOU’s stick and the puck is now loose toward the side boards. D1 is farther inside. The scene begins after the missed reception.
cues: YOU do not currently own the puck.
The loose puck is wider than YOU.
The original receiving spot is no longer the puck location.

The next read becomes defending or regaining possession

scene.title: Angle the carrier away from the slot
scene.objective: Use an inside approach to influence a wide carrier without assuming a forced turnover.
scene.briefing: Navy attacks the right net (+x); gold attacks the left net. YOU are gold and defend the right goal. F1 carries toward the half wall on the same side. F2 waits across the slot. Consider an approach that limits the route into the middle.
cues: YOU start closer to the middle than F1.
F1 is wide near the half-wall side.
F2 remains a possible cross-ice receiver.
